LoloBuy additional parcel payment: match the request to the final package

A LoloBuy additional parcel payment can appear when the packed shipment costs more than the amount paid from the earlier estimate. The current warehouse guidance explains that initial parcel payment is based on estimated chargeable weight. After packing, actual weight or volume is confirmed. If the final shipping amount differs, LoloBuy says the buyer may be notified through an in-site message to pay the difference or receive a refund.

That does not mean every request should be paid immediately. First establish that it belongs to your package, that the final measurements explain the change and that the Bill record identifies it as a parcel transaction. A product-order replenishment, balance recharge and parcel replenishment are different records.

This checklist focuses on one decision: how to verify an additional parcel payment before you authorize it, while avoiding duplicate charges and unsupported assumptions.

1. Confirm that the request belongs to the correct package

Start in My packages and open the package named in the message. Match its package number, item list, destination country, shipping method and submission time with your own records. If you submitted several parcels close together, do not rely on the first product image or a similar amount.

Keep the package number separate from the original product order number, warehouse item number, rehearsal number, waybill number and payment transaction number. The package number identifies the shipment record. A bill can then carry a separate business number and transaction number that link the financial event to that shipment.

If the notice does not identify a package, or the item list and destination do not match, pause. Save the notice and ask support which package number and bill number the request belongs to before paying.

2. Compare estimated and final parcel data

The current Package Details page distinguishes estimated shipping from final shipping after weigh-in. It can also show estimated chargeable weight, final chargeable weight, the earlier deposit and an Amount Due. Read these values together instead of looking only at the new amount.

Create a four-line record: estimated chargeable weight, final chargeable weight, estimated shipping and final shipping. Then note any displayed discount, service, handling, insurance, customs, fuel or tax component. Do not add a fee merely because it exists on another parcel; use only the components shown for this package.

If a value is missing, label it “not shown” rather than estimating it yourself. A screenshot of the full freight comparison is stronger evidence than a cropped Amount Due figure.

3. Understand why packed weight can change the charge

Stored-item weight is not necessarily the final billing figure. Packaging materials, retained retail boxes, protective services and the completed parcel dimensions can change the outbound measurement. A route may charge by actual weight, volumetric weight or the greater of the two.

For a light but large parcel, the volumetric result may be more important than the scale weight. For a dense parcel, actual weight may remain the billing basis. LoloBuy’s freight estimator can display the billing standard and a route-specific volumetric formula, so do not apply one universal divisor copied from an older guide.

Check whether the final chargeable weight is consistent with the line’s stated method. This does not require deciding whether the carrier is right or wrong; it requires identifying which measurement produced the bill.

4. Distinguish package replenishment from other payments

LoloBuy’s current transaction labels include Package payment, Package replenishment, Parcel refund, Order payment, Order replenishment and Balance recharge. Similar words can refer to different business stages. An international parcel difference should not be verified against a product-order bill alone.

Open Bill and look for the transaction type, business number, transaction number, transaction time, business amount, channel information and status. Match the business reference to the package record. The reason field, when shown, should explain why replenishment is required.

Do not treat a bank notification as the authoritative description of the LoloBuy transaction. The bank may show an authorization or settlement reference, while the platform bill shows which business event the payment is meant to cover. You need both when investigating a discrepancy.

5. Reconcile the amount before choosing a payment method

Use the package page and Bill record to reconstruct the difference. The simplest check is final package amount minus the parcel amount already credited, adjusted only by discounts or fees that the account explicitly lists. Your result should align with Amount Due or the replenishment amount.

If it does not align, check whether you compared the same currency and whether a channel fee is separate. Payment screens can show a payment method, total payable and handling fee. Currency conversion and payment-channel charges are not the same as the parcel freight difference, so keep them in separate rows.

Do not use a remembered exchange rate or a screenshot from another day. Record the currency and values shown at the time you review the live payment screen. If the explanation remains unclear, ask for a breakdown before completing payment.

6. Prevent duplicate parcel payments

Before retrying, check the bill status and transaction history. LoloBuy currently uses states such as Pending payment, Paid, Completed, Cancelled, Pending refund and Error. A pending state does not prove failure, while a bank authorization does not by itself prove that the platform marked the replenishment Paid.

Save the first transaction number, payment method, amount and timestamp. Refresh the Bill record and package page before starting another attempt. If the bank shows a debit but LoloBuy still shows Pending payment or Error, contact support with both references instead of immediately creating a second charge.

Never send a password, verification code, full card number or security code in a support message. A package number, bill number, transaction number, amount, timestamp and redacted bank evidence are usually the relevant identifiers.

7. Handle the refund side as a separate transaction

If final shipping is lower than the credited estimate, LoloBuy’s current guidance says a refund notice may be sent through an in-site message. The Bill system separately labels Parcel refund and Pending refund. Do not assume that a lower final amount has already reached your external payment account.

Match the parcel refund to the same package business number and record its status, amount and transaction time. Also distinguish a parcel refund from a product-order refund, original return or account-balance movement. These may appear in the same financial area but represent different events.

No universal posting time or destination should be inferred. Preserve the platform record and compare it with the relevant payment or balance statement. If they disagree, report the exact two records rather than saying only that “the refund is missing.”

8. Write one support request that can be audited

Collect the package number, item list, shipping method, estimated and final chargeable weights, estimated and final shipping amounts, Amount Due, bill number, transaction number and in-site message. Add screenshots that show field labels as well as values.

A clear message might say: “Package [number] shows estimated chargeable weight [shown value] and final chargeable weight [shown value]. Final shipping is [shown amount], and Bill [number] requests Package replenishment of [shown amount]. Please confirm the calculation and whether transaction [number] is the only outstanding payment for this package.”

If the amount cannot be reconciled, ask which measurement, service or fee created the difference. If you already attempted payment, include the first transaction reference and ask for its platform status. Keep one conversation thread so the evidence remains chronological.

Final LoloBuy additional parcel payment checklist

Confirm the correct package, compare estimated and final measurements, identify the route’s billing basis and review every displayed freight component. Then match the request to a Bill entry labelled for the parcel, with the correct business number, transaction number, amount and status.

Separate freight difference, payment-channel fee and currency conversion. Check for an existing pending or paid transaction before retrying, and track any parcel refund independently. A verified record does not eliminate every shipping adjustment, but it prevents a legitimate estimate change from being confused with the wrong bill or a duplicate payment.
